title: Path Sum
statement: Return True if some root-to-LEAF path has values that add up to targetSum. A leaf is a node with no children.

hints.1_question: You need a path that ends at a leaf. What should you do when you reach a node that is not a leaf?
hints.2_nudge: Subtract each node's value from the target as you go down. At a leaf, check whether the remaining target equals the leaf's value.
hints.3_big_hint: if not root: False; if leaf: return root.val == t; return hasPathSum(left, t - root.val) or hasPathSum(right, t - root.val).

known_bugs.name: accepts a path that ends at any node
known_bugs.followup: For the tree [1, 2] and target 1, the root alone sums to 1. Is the root a leaf?

known_bugs.name: empty tree with target 0 is True
known_bugs.followup: Is there a root-to-leaf path in an empty tree?

known_bugs.name: prunes when the running sum exceeds the target (assumes positives)
known_bugs.followup: If values can be negative, can a sum that is too big now come back down to the target later?

followups: What changes if the path may start and end at any node (problem 437)?
Why is it important that the check happens only at leaves?
